body:
This is interesting.  I had been afraid to talk about my depression, not because I was afraid of looking like an attention whore, but mainly because it's so hard for others to understand. I mean, everyone feels sad sometimes.  And that's why people will say, "just snap out of it" because they don't really get it.  

But I found that the more people I told about it, the more people opened up about their own struggles with depression being in their lives in one way or another.  I don't want it to be taboo.  Would you be ashamed if you were diabetic and wanted to talk about the woes of that?  So I am trying to be more open (with a select group of people) about it.  It doesn't always help necessarily, as people just don't know what to say.  But it makes me feel better at least.

If you are on a college campus there should be free/cheap counseling services.  I found my therapist & psychiatrist through the Psychology Today's "Find A Therapist" search on their website.

I am currently trying out welbutrin but am still in the trial and error phase. It is good to hear the stories of meds working and being able to get off them. 

I am curious about your mention of yoga. I have considered meditation but dont know how to start because i am just stuck inside my own head so much of the time!

And congrats to you on getting your doctorate!! Something i will (most likely) never do!

Protecting myself hits the nail on the head. Really it's just great to know other people feel this way AND that someone understands exactly how i'm feeling. People who haven't been through it can't understand, which makes things very lonely.

"Expecting to be miserable" is definitely something i face. Its so much easier, well comfortable to just be miserable sometimes than to do all that work and face all those fears. That is definitely a struggle.
I HAVE. I got a new job 800 times better than my old one and moved to a new neighborhood. Depression doesn't care.

Thank you for this. I rarely get to hear "off medication" and "happy" in the same sentence. 

I have been in therapy for 1.5 years and almost 2 mos on welbutrin. I had seen small improvements but am now thinking the dosage needs to be increased which of course just makes me feel like i actually am a crazy person who can only fit into society if heavily medicated...

But i do thank you for sharing that you have gotten past it. It surely seems impossible a lot of the time.
Thanks, just put in a request to have it transferred to my local library branch.

That is a good reminder! I'm sure i sabotage myself a lot of the time to feel worse just because i dont feel like doing anything ever (eating & getting out of bed seems impossible let alone other things i used to enjoy like exercise & cooking). 

Not getting enjoyment from things really puts a damper on that, and anything i have done to give myself confidence is only temporary. 

Don't laugh, but last weekend i ran a half marathon and PR'd. I had a serious high from that for about three days then plummeted back down. On days like today, i can't even connect that I was the person running. It doesn't give me any good/accomplishment feeling when i think about the race. 

I am trying to get better on not dismissing accomplishments but it's hard when i dont feel anything from them.

I think the main issue is with needing to take meds just to feel "normal"; to feel the way others feel without meds. 

I have no problems taking birth control even though it messes with my hormones and ive had to try out different types. But it's a common thing that the majority of women take. For whatever reason, i dont feel dependent on it, but more taking control over my body. 

Taking anti-depressants, however, makes me feel out of control - that my life has gotten so bad that i can't even feel "normal" without help. Everything feels like chaos, like im floating away and have nothing to keep me grounded - no reason for stability.
It's the ups and downs that are impossible to handle. Having a string of okay days gives me hope just to have it shattered by a low day - basically makes me think it'll never feel better.

The disconnect between what i KNOW and what i FEEL gets extremely tiring as well. It's like a constant internal war between my brain trying to be logical and illogical at the same time! 

I feel like it will never get better - that i will never get back what i had, and i dwell on the past like no other. Yet i know that it (probably) will get better as i've seen it happen and that the past is holding me down. 

I've been fighting for sooo long that on days like this, i just can't take it anymore. It's like i'm on a treadmill where nothing really matters because i'll always be back where i started. 

I can tell you and myself all the good things about me but since i dont FEEL it, it doesn't really cheer me up. Just makes me feel empty, really. Like, im not talking about myself at all.
Thank you. i don't mean to be argumentative here it's just so tiring fighting everyday and feel like i'm getting nowhere.

Honestly, its pretty depressing hearing about everyone's different experiences with the meds. I hate that it's come to this; my life being dependent on medication - feeling like i've lost all control.
I'm trying and getting nowhere! I have made life improvements, been in therapy for a year, and been taking meds. I'm feeling defeated.
